title: Ops utility catalog: provenance & handoff for runbooks-as-microtasks
creator: Mina Khatri
description:
Summary:
We need a standardized ops-utility catalog that attaches provenance (what generated a runbook / microtask, which version, who reviewed it) and a lightweight handoff protocol so that on-call engineers and automated remediators can adopt runbooks-as-tasks reliably. This ticket scopes a minimal, audit-friendly metadata envelope, UI listing in the Admin Tools catalog, and a sampling telemetry pipeline to track usage and safety regressions.
background: Operational context: Over the last year we accumulated dozens of ad-hoc runbooks and small remediation scripts in multiple repos and in Confluence. Engineers are unsure which artifact is authoritative, whether a runbook was dry-run tested, and which rollout or patch introduced a change. That uncertainty increases incident MTTR and blocks safe automation (we cannot automatically execute anything unless provenance and review metadata exists).
goals: 1) Define a minimal metadata schema for ops-microtasks that covers provenance (origin repo/PR/build), review state, required IAM role, and rollback steps. 2) Surface catalog entries in Admin Tools with search/filter and quick preview. 3) Emit telemetry events for execution attempts, dry-run results, and safety exceptions to Sentry/Datadog. 4) Provide a CLI and API for creating/updating catalog entries and for the handoff workflow when an engineer upgrades a runbook.
non_goals: Full RBAC across all tenants (we will integrate existing RBAC later), migrating every legacy runbook into the catalog, and building a visual authoring tool in this phase.
constraints_risks:
- Any automated execution path must include a safety-check gate; false positives could prevent remediation.
- Telemetry must not leak sensitive customer data; redact parameters before emitting.
- Adding catalog checks to CI may add latency.
- Requires coordination with Security for KMS/secret handling when runbooks reference credentials.
proposal:
Deliverables in this iteration:
- Metadata schema (JSON envelope) with fields: name, key, version, origin_repo, origin_pr, author, reviewers, approvals, dry_run_sha, safe_to_automate (enum), required_roles, last_tested_at, rollback_instructions, tags.
- A small admin-catalog React surface (cards + quick-preview) plugged into the Console.
- A CLI command `redwood ops catalog add|update|promote` that records PR linkage and approval IDs.
- Telemetry: events 'ops.catalog.register', 'ops.catalog.execute_attempt', 'ops.catalog.dryrun_result' with redaction rules.
- Acceptance: runbook created via CLI appears in Console, has provenance links to GitHub PR, and an example dry-run emits telemetry and shows up in the dashboard.
tradeoffs:
- We keep the envelope intentionally small to avoid long approval cycles; richer metadata can be added later.
- Catalog entries will not be the single source of truth initially — we will provide warnings for legacy artifacts rather than blocking them.
- Storing a copy of the runbook in the catalog vs. storing only pointers: we will start with pointers to avoid duplication and sync complexity.
design_notes: UI: list view + compact preview with provenance links and last-tested badge. Include an 'automate' toggle visible only to RBAC-permitted users. The quick preview shows last dry-run logs (sanitized) and the last approving PR. See mock: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1MockCatalogMockup (internal).
implementation_plan: Week 1: finalize schema, add GitHub PR link extractor in CLI. Week 2: build minimal Console listing and wire telemetry. Week 3: integrate dry-run pipeline and safety checks; run internal dogfood. Week 4: polish, docs, and RFC + rollout to alpha group.
metrics:
Primary: catalog registrations/week, executions via catalog, dry-run pass rate, number of incidents where cataloged runbook reduced MTTR. Safety metric: percent of automated executions that hit manual-review flag.
Dashboards: ops-catalog - registrations by team, dry-run failures.
acceptance_criteria: A runbook added via CLI (with a GitHub PR link) appears in the Console catalog card.
Dry-run results are emitted as telemetry and visible in the dashboard within 5 minutes.
At least two existing runbooks are migrated as pointers and marked with provenance info.
Security sign-off obtained for redaction rules and KMS usage (or documented exception).
